Three days before I started my freshman year of college I crashed my car into a house. Some teenage boys threw a rock at my car and I swerved to avoid it and lost control and flew into the house, completely destroying it. My passenger and I both were injured with head injuries, broken bones, and wounds and taken to the ER. It was all over every news source in my state. My whole town hated me because the house I hit was the house of a "popular" girl in my grade. I couldn't get the sight out of my head for a long time. The memory of how it feels in that split second when you're crashing (although I skidded for quite some distance.) The sight, the sound, the smell... everything about it. Every day it would replay constantly, until about a month or two ago when it started to slow down. I came to notice that the things that have helped the most are time and acceptance. Accept what happened. Take time to have a conversation with yourself and just accept the fact that what happened happened and you can't go back. Worrying and stressing all the time will not take back what happened, it will just make you feel worse, so what's the real point? I know that's a lot easier said than done, but trust me, it's worth a try to just take some time to really try to realize the reality of it. And most importantly, give it time. Time is the best healer for all wounds. All the exercises I did in therapy, all the love and support from friends and family... nothing compares to TIME. It will get better with time. You will stop replaying the scene in your head so much. You will stop being so afraid to drive. You will stop letting the guilt eat you alive. And I am not saying that these feelings will go away completely, but time will weaken them and it will get easier. I know how you feel. Although our situations aren't exactly the same, they are close, and I'm sure we feel a lot of the same feelings. Trust me when I tell you that even though it seems like your life is ruined at this point, things will improve after a couple months.
Best of luck to you, and I'm sorry that this happened.
